references.text: Reuben tore his clothes in grief, a similar expression of deep sorrow and despair as Joshua showed.
Jacob tore his clothes when he heard about Joseph's presumed death, the same expression of grief that Joshua used.
Joshua and Caleb tore their clothes when the people refused to enter Canaan, the same action as in this verse.
Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before the Lord's glory, a similar act of humility before God.
A man from Benjamin came with dust on his head to show grief over Israel's defeat, the same action as Joshua and the elders.
A man came to David with dust on his head to show grief, the same expression of sorrow used here.
Tamar put ashes on her head in grief, a similar act to scattering dust on one's head.
Job tore his robe and fell to the ground in worship after hearing about his losses, a similar reaction to disaster.
Job's friends threw dust toward heaven over their heads as a sign of grief, the same action as Joshua and the elders.
The elders in Zion scattered dust on their heads in the lament over Jerusalem's destruction, the same expression of sorrow.
The sailors cast dust on their heads in grief over Tyre's fall, the same act of mourning.
